gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each 2-bay NAS costs to run per year for Time Machine duty. Using each maker's own access and hibernation wattage over 8 h of drive access and 16 h of hibernation a day, at the EIA's August 2026 US residential average of 18.16¢/kWh, the result ranges from about $9.37 a year (QNAP TS-233) and $10.78 (UGREEN DH2300) through $12.89–15.45 for the three Synology models to $23.33 (TerraMaster F2-425).
standout_why: I checked the two cited pages. Apple's 'Backup disks you can use with Time Machine' (support.apple.com/en-us/102423) gives no power, speed or sizing figures; it only says to use SMB and that AFP isn't supported in macOS 27 or later. Synology's Time Machine KB tutorial gives no figures either. Synology's compare page (result 4) lists raw access and hibernation watts for DS223, DS223j and DS225+, so part of the input is in ChatGPT's results. None of its results turns those watts into kWh or dollars a year, and none covers UGREEN, QNAP or TerraMaster. UGREEN's own blog works out yearly cost only for its own models, and ChatGPT didn't get that page.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's point that the DS223 is enough for backups only. Its running cost is about $13.52 a year, against $15.45 for the DS225+, so electricity barely separates the Synology models and doesn't change the pick between them. It does mark down the TerraMaster F2-425: its 11 W hibernation figure gives about $23.33 a year, roughly $117 over 5 years, versus $54 for the UGREEN DH2300 and $47 for the QNAP TS-233. That puts the DH2300 ($239.99 + $53.90 ≈ $294 over 5 years) ahead as the low-running-cost choice where a price is sourced. The differences are $5–14 a year, so this is a tiebreaker, not the main reason to pick a model.

findings.label: Caveat on comparing these figures
findings.note: Synology points to a KB article for its method. UGREEN tested with Seagate 2 TB drives, TerraMaster with Seagate 4 TB ST4000VN008, and QNAP only says 'drives fully populated'. The drives you install will move every figure. Treat gaps of a few dollars a year as ties. Only the F2-425 vs TS-233/DH2300 gap (about $12–14/yr) stands out.
